### Guilty of Brutishness
Author: Alistair Begg
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/truth-for-life/truth-for-life-july-28-2021.html
Passage: Psalm 73:22
Points:
- Asaph openly confesses his inner folly and envy regarding the temporary prosperity of the wicked.
- Believers act pridefully whenever they assume they are immune to similar sinful attitudes.
- We often misinterpret God's providences in dark times, failing to see that trials work for our good.
- Acknowledging our spiritual foolishness should cause us to rely completely on God's wise guidance.

### Before My Feet Hit the Floor
Author: Rachel Wojo
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/encouragement/encouragement-for-today-august-26-2026.html
Passage: Psalm 73:26
Points:
- Chronic pain, exhaustion, and grief can make facing a new day feel overwhelming and impossible.
- Asaph was transparent about nearly losing his faith when comparing his afflictions to the ease of others.
- The decisive turning point occurs when we realize our human limitations are met by God's enduring strength.
- Surrendering our weakness to God before starting the day reminds us that the battle belongs to Him.

### The Beast I Become: How to Bring Bitterness to God
Author: Scott Hubbard
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/the-beast-i-become
Passage: Psalm 73:23-24
Points:
- Unanswered prayers and unexpected loss can cause grief to curdle into beastly bitterness toward God.
- Renewal begins when we realize God has not abandoned us and is continually holding our right hand.
- The Lord directs us through the wilderness of suffering by the trustworthy counsel of His Word.
- Remembering that God will receive us into glory gives an eternal perspective that disarms present grief.

### Devotional: Psalm 73
Author: D. A. Carson
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/devotionals/read-the-bible/numbers-29-psalm-73-isaiah-21-2-peter-2/
Passage: Psalm 73:1-28
Points:
- Observing the apparent serenity and wealth of the ungodly can destabilize a believer's moral balance.
- Asaph wrestled with the temptation to conclude that living a life of purity was entirely futile.
- Entering God's sanctuary shifted his perspective by exposing the sudden ruin that awaits the wicked.
- The believer possesses an infinitely greater inheritance through unbroken fellowship with God both now and in glory.
- Repenting of envy and bitterness leads to a renewed commitment to draw near to God and proclaim His deeds.
